closing.message: The Registrars of Voters are thankful for the dedication of all who assist Greenwich voters at every election.

cards.q: Who is the most important person at the election?
cards.a: The voter. Everything is based on providing the registered voter with the best possible experience.

cards.q: What are the official hours of voting on election day?
cards.a: On election day all polling places are open from 6AM to 8PM.

cards.q: Who must be sworn in by the Moderator before starting work?
cards.a: All election officials must be sworn in prior to the start of the election.

cards.q: Can a poll worker wear a t-shirt or pin supporting a candidate?
cards.a: No. Poll workers must remain non-partisan and cannot wear or display any political materials.

cards.q: What does the "75-foot sign" signify?
cards.a: The boundary within which no campaigning or political discussion is allowed. It is measured in an arc from the exterior polling place doors.

cards.q: Who is allowed inside the polling place?
cards.a: Voters who are voting, members of the press, election officials, credentialed representatives from the Secretary of the State and individuals assisting a voter.

cards.q: What is the IVS system?
cards.a: The Inspire Voting System is the accessible ballot marking device available for any voter who wishes to use it.

cards.q: Can a child enter the voting booth with a parent?
cards.a: Yes, a child may accompany a parent into the voting booth. The parent, however, must insert their own ballot in the tabulator.

cards.q: What is Same Day Registration (SDR)?
cards.a: The process that allows an unregistered voter to register and vote at a designated SDR location (Town Hall). Voters who are not registered MUST come to Town Hall to take advantage of this.

cards.q: What must be displayed on a wall for all voters to see?
cards.a: A sample ballot and six large informational posters, including the "Voters Bill of Rights."

cards.q: What is the purpose of the Moderator's Diary?
cards.a: To record any unusual occurrences, from machine jams to disruptive voters, to help improve future elections.

cards.q: If a voter needs assistance due to a disability or language barrier, what is the procedure?
cards.a: Notify the Moderator. Two election officials of differing parties will assist the voter.

cards.q: What are the acceptable forms of ID a voter can present?
cards.a: A pre-printed ID with their name and address; name and signature; OR name and photograph.

cards.q: A voter is on the Active list but has no ID. What is the procedure?
cards.a: The voter must sign the Form "Signatory Affidavit for Voters Who Do Not Present ID."

cards.q: A voter is on the Inactive List. What must they do to be restored and vote?
cards.a: They must show a current and valid ID, and complete a new voter registration card.

cards.q: What does the letter "A" in red or blue next to a voter's name signify?
cards.a: The voter has already cast an Absentee Ballot. This voter cannot vote in person.

cards.q: At the polls, a voter needs to change their address within Greenwich. What do you do?
cards.a: Direct them to the Assistant Registrar or the Moderator, who will have them complete a new voter registration card.

cards.q: What do you write next to the name of a voter who casts a Provisional Ballot?
cards.a: "PB" Do NOT cross out the name.

cards.q: What do you write next to the name of a voter who casts a Challenge Ballot?
cards.a: "CB" Do NOT cross out the name.

cards.q: A voter presents a State of CT Confidentiality Card. Where is their name found?
cards.a: On the last page of the Official Checker book. You must not ask for their address.

cards.q: What is the purpose of the tally sheet at the checker's table?
cards.a: To make a hash mark for every voter processed, which is used for the hourly count reconciliation.

cards.q: What is the Supplemental List?
cards.a: A list of voters who have registered or made changes to their registration close to Election Day, after the main registry list was printed.

cards.q: If a voter provides a driver's license with an old address, is it valid?
cards.a: Yes, ID does not need to have the voter's current address. At the polling place ID is used to verify identity, not residency.

cards.q: A voter has moved from another town in CT and is not on your list. What should you do?
cards.a: Direct them to Town Hall for Same Day Registration (SDR).

cards.q: Who is responsible for placing the blue "A"s next to the names of absentee voters?
cards.a: The Moderator will periodically instruct the Official Checker to do this based on updates from the Registrars of Voters.

cards.q: What must a Ballot Clerk give to every voter along with their ballot?
cards.a: A privacy sleeve. Please check to make sure the sleeve is empty.

cards.q: What is a "spoiled" ballot?
cards.a: A ballot that a voter makes a mistake on and returns to the Ballot Clerk to be replaced with a fresh ballot.

cards.q: How many replacement ballots can a single voter receive?
cards.a: A voter can receive as many replacements as they need.

cards.q: What must the Ballot Clerk do with a spoiled ballot?
cards.a: Place it in the "Spoiled Ballot Envelope" and record it on the appropriate tally sheet.

cards.q: How does the ballot clerk keep track of the number of ballots issued?
cards.a: By using a tally sheet, making a hash mark for every ballot given to a voter.

cards.q: What should the Ballot Clerk do with the tally sheet at the end of the night?
cards.a: Total the number of ballots issued and give the sheet to the Moderator as part of the closing reconciliation.

cards.q: A ballot jams, but the screen shows a GREEN checkmark. Has the ballot been counted?
cards.a: Yes. The vote was successfully counted. Call the Moderator to clear the jam.

cards.q: A ballot jams, but the screen shows a RED X. Has the ballot been counted?
cards.a: No. The vote was NOT counted. Call the Moderator immediately.

cards.q: How far away should the tabulator tender stand from the tabulator?
cards.a: At least 4 feet away to protect voter privacy.

cards.q: What should the tabulator tender do with used privacy sleeves?
cards.a: Periodically collect them and return them to the ballot clerk's table. Make certain they are EMPTY.

cards.q: What is the most important rule for a tabulator tender regarding a voter's ballot?
cards.a: Never look at it. The voter's right to a secret ballot is paramount.

cards.q: If the tabulator screen displays a message you don't understand, what should you do?
cards.a: Call the Moderator immediately.

cards.q: When can you leave your station unattended?
cards.a: Never. You may leave your station only when you have been relieved for a break by another election official.

cards.q: What is the Moderator's ultimate responsibility at the polling place?
cards.a: To ensure the election is conducted fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with all state laws and procedures.

cards.q: What must be verified before cutting the seals on the Big Blue Bin?
cards.a: The seal numbers must match the numbers on the Certificate for Opening of the Polls in the Moderator Return.

cards.q: How many copies of the results tape are printed at the end of the night, and where do they go?
cards.a: Three copies. One is returned to the ROVs, one is posted on the wall for the public, and one is placed inside the used ballot bag.

cards.q: How many copies of the zero tape are printed in the morning, and where do they go?
cards.a: Three copies. One is returned to the ROVs, one is posted on the wall for the public, and one is placed inside the used ballot bag.

cards.q: What is the process for a hand count of ballots from the auxiliary bin?
cards.a: The count must be done by two officials of different parties, and the results recorded on the Hand Count Tally Sheet.

cards.q: If the tabulator malfunctions, who must be called immediately?
cards.a: The Registrar of Voters' office. We will send out an additional tabulator to replace malfunctioning equipment.

cards.q: What is the role of the Special Assistant Registrar (SAR)?
cards.a: The SAR is to assist the Moderator with the setup of the tabulators and the IVS system. At night they will assist with packing up the equipment.

cards.q: Who is ultimately in charge of the polling place and has the final say on all procedural decisions?
cards.a: The Moderator.

cards.q: How many days of early voting are there for a November election?
cards.a: There are 14 consecutive days ending on the Sunday before Election Day.

cards.q: How many days of early voting are there for a party primary?
cards.a: There are 7 consecutive days ending on the Sunday before the Primary.

cards.q: What are the rules for press who want to enter a polling place?
cards.a: The Moderator may grant permission, but they are not allowed to record a voter's marked ballot or disrupt the voting process.

cards.q: What is the purpose of the IVS Startup Report that is printed in the morning?
cards.a: It verifies that the accessible voting machine has been set up correctly. It must be signed by the SAR and Moderator.

cards.q: A voter wants to cast a "write-in" vote. Where do they write the name of the candidate?
cards.a: The voter writes the name on the write-in line and fills in the oval. The name must appear under the specific office for which the candidate is running.

cards.q: During the hourly count, what numbers must be reconciled?
cards.a: The public counter on the tabulator, the official checker's tally sheet, and the ballot clerk's tally sheet should all match.
